claim_text: The HST/WFC3 transmission spectrum of WASP-12 b contains a high-confidence water absorption signal.
supporting_evidence: Six HST/WFC3 transit observations spanning 0.84-1.67 microns, binned into 13 spectrophotometric light curves with a median transit-depth precision of 51 ppm, yield a 7 sigma water detection.
assumptions: the transmission-spectrum systematics are adequately corrected
the retrieval opacity model for water is appropriate
uncertainty: Water absorption is reported at 7 sigma confidence; the retrieved water volume mixing ratio spans 10^-5 to 10^-2 at 1 sigma.

claim_text: An equilibrium-chemistry retrieval of WASP-12 b favors a near-solar carbon-to-oxygen ratio and rules out a carbon-rich atmosphere.
supporting_evidence: A retrieval parameterization fitting carbon-to-oxygen ratio and metallicity under chemical equilibrium gives C/O = 0.5 with asymmetric 1 sigma errors and excludes C/O greater than 1 at more than 3 sigma.
assumptions: chemical equilibrium
the adopted metallicity and opacity parameterization is adequate
the transmission spectrum samples a representative terminator composition
uncertainty: C/O is constrained to 0.5(+0.2,-0.3) at 1 sigma; C/O greater than 1 is ruled out at greater than 3 sigma.

claim_text: For clear solar-composition transiting exoplanet atmospheres, JWST transmission spectra from 1 to 2.5 microns can often constrain the major molecular constituents.
supporting_evidence: Simulated single-transit spectra and retrievals for archetypal hot-Jupiter, warm-Neptune, warm-sub-Neptune, and cool-super-Earth atmospheres across several JWST modes recover major species in clear solar-composition cases.
assumptions: the simulated instrument noise is representative of on-orbit JWST performance
the archetypal atmospheric models span the relevant planet classes
the retrieval model is not strongly misspecified
uncertainty: The paper states this will occur often rather than universally and notes that actual on-orbit performance was not yet known.

claim_text: Cloudy or high-mean-molecular-weight atmospheres generally require broader 1 to 11 micron JWST coverage than clear atmospheres to obtain good constraints.
supporting_evidence: Retrievals on simulated cloudy and high-mean-molecular-weight transmission and emission spectra show weaker constraints in narrow wavelength ranges and improved constraints when full 1-11 micron coverage is used.
assumptions: the adopted cloud and high-mean-molecular-weight models are representative
the simulated noise and observing modes are realistic
the retrieval parameterization matches the simulated atmospheres
uncertainty: The conclusion is framed as an expectation that applies often, not to every atmosphere.

claim_text: A two-dimensional retrieval with inhomogeneous clouds finds evidence for nitrogen-bearing chemistry in the atmosphere of HD 209458 b.
supporting_evidence: A fully Bayesian exploration of 10^8 models spanning cloud-free to fully cloudy cases yields combined NH3 and/or HCN evidence at 3.7-7.7 sigma and NH3 detections of 3.3-4.9 sigma depending on cloud assumptions.
assumptions: the two-dimensional cloud prescription captures the dominant terminator inhomogeneity
the molecular opacity database is accurate
the Bayesian model comparison is appropriately calibrated
uncertainty: Detection significance varies from 3.7 to 7.7 sigma for NH3 and/or HCN and from 3.3 to 4.9 sigma for NH3 under different cloud scenarios.

claim_text: The preferred retrieval for HD 209458 b indicates non-uniform cloud coverage, high-altitude haze, and strongly subsolar water abundance at the terminator.
supporting_evidence: The highest-evidence model gives non-uniform clouds at 4.5-5.4 sigma, hazes above 3 sigma, and H2O at 5-15 ppm, corresponding to 0.01-0.03 times solar.
assumptions: the selected highest-evidence model is physically adequate
the stellar and instrumental systematics are sufficiently controlled
the adopted cloud geometry is flexible enough
uncertainty: Cloud and water significances depend on the assumed cloud distribution; the water constraint is 5-15 ppm.

claim_text: Stellar heterogeneity in M dwarfs can imprint contamination signals in rocky-planet transmission spectra that exceed the expected planetary atmospheric features by more than an order of magnitude.
supporting_evidence: Models of spot and facula covering fractions consistent with observed M-dwarf variability produce contamination spectra more than 10 times larger than expected atmospheric transit-depth changes.
assumptions: the modeled spot and facula temperature contrasts are representative
photometric variability constrains plausible covering fractions
the planetary atmospheric feature amplitudes used for comparison are representative
uncertainty: The claim is based on modeled plausible ranges because direct constraints on M-dwarf photospheric heterogeneity are limited.

claim_text: For the TRAPPIST-1 system, stellar contamination can alter atmospheric-species transit depths by roughly 1 to 15 times the expected planetary signal and bias inferred planet densities low.
supporting_evidence: TRAPPIST-1 rotational variability is fit by broad spot and facula covering-fraction ranges whose contamination spectra produce 1-15 times the planetary feature strength and density biases centered near an 8 percent underestimate.
assumptions: the adopted photospheric heterogeneity model represents TRAPPIST-1
the rotational variability constrains the relevant spot and facula configurations
the same stellar surface state applies during the modeled transits
uncertainty: Spot and facula fractions have large asymmetric uncertainties; the density bias is reported as -8 percent with a range of approximately -20 to +7 percent.

claim_text: A homogeneous retrieval analysis finds that most of the ten hot Jupiters studied have day-night terminator water abundances consistent with subsolar values.
supporting_evidence: Retrievals of the full sample yield best-constrained log water abundances from about -5.04 to -3.16, corresponding to roughly 0.018 to 1.40 times solar under equilibrium-chemistry expectations.
assumptions: the retrieval framework is comparably valid across the full sample
solar-abundance equilibrium chemistry is an appropriate reference
cloud and haze parameterizations capture the dominant degeneracies
uncertainty: Individual abundance posteriors are broad and one upper range includes solar values; the conclusion is stated for the majority of the sample.
datasets: Transmission spectra of ten hot Jupiters

claim_text: The retrieved hot-Jupiter water abundances imply either subsolar oxygen abundance, supersolar carbon-to-oxygen ratio, or a combination of both.
supporting_evidence: The homogeneous retrievals produce water abundances below solar-equilibrium expectations for much of the sample after jointly fitting cloud and haze properties.
assumptions: equilibrium-chemistry expectations provide a valid baseline
retrieved water is representative of bulk atmospheric composition
other processes such as disequilibrium chemistry do not dominate the discrepancy
uncertainty: The interpretation is non-unique because low water can arise from subsolar oxygen, high C/O, or both.
datasets: Transmission spectra of ten hot Jupiters

claim_text: Applying one-dimensional retrieval models to spectra from atmospheres with different morning and evening terminator compositions can produce spuriously cold retrieved temperatures.
supporting_evidence: Synthetic multidimensional terminator spectra fitted with one-dimensional models yield acceptable spectral fits but temperatures hundreds of kelvin too low and weaker-than-true temperature gradients.
assumptions: the simulated morning-evening compositional contrasts are representative
the one-dimensional retrieval setup reflects common practice
the forward models capture the relevant opacity and thermal structure
uncertainty: Bias magnitude varies with planet and composition; reported errors can approach about 1000 K in observed retrieval anomalies.

claim_text: One-dimensional retrievals of heterogeneous terminators can bias retrieved molecular abundances, including water, by more than an order of magnitude.
supporting_evidence: Retrieval experiments show most abundances displaced by more than 1 sigma, some by more than 3 sigma, and the strongest water biases exceeding a factor of ten for ultra-hot Jupiters.
assumptions: the modeled terminator heterogeneity resembles real planets
the retrieval priors do not dominate the inferred bias
the opacity sources used in the simulations are complete enough
uncertainty: The strongest biases occur for ultra-hot Jupiters and depend on which opacity sources differ between morning and evening limbs.
datasets: Published retrievals of WASP-12 b and WASP-17 b

claim_text: High-resolution HARPS transmission spectroscopy resolves the sodium D doublet in the atmosphere of HD 189733 b at high significance.
supporting_evidence: Archival HARPS transit observations yield D2 and D1 line contrasts of 0.64 plus or minus 0.07 percent and 0.40 plus or minus 0.07 percent, corresponding to a 10 sigma excess-absorption detection.
assumptions: telluric and orbital-motion corrections are adequate
stellar line variations do not mimic the sodium signal
the passband-based significance calculation is valid
uncertainty: The excess absorption is 0.32 plus or minus 0.03 percent in the adopted passband, reported at 10 sigma.

claim_text: The resolved sodium lines in HD 189733 b indicate hotter upper-atmosphere layers and a possible high-altitude wind blueshift.
supporting_evidence: Isothermal-model comparisons give temperatures of 2600 plus or minus 600 K and 3270 plus or minus 330 K at the D1 and D2 line-core altitudes, while the line centers are blueshifted by 0.16 plus or minus 0.04 angstrom.
assumptions: isothermal models map line-core widths to atmospheric temperature reliably
the line-position offset is not caused by residual calibration or stellar effects
the blueshift can be interpreted as bulk atmospheric motion
uncertainty: The blueshift is a 4 sigma measurement; the inferred wind speed is 8 plus or minus 2 km/s and is presented as a possible interpretation.

claim_text: Within the HST/WFC3 bandpass, fractional cloud coverage can exactly mimic a cloud-free high-mean-molecular-weight atmosphere.
supporting_evidence: Analytic modeling and retrievals of synthetic spectra show that patchy solar-composition clouds and cloud-free high-mean-molecular-weight atmospheres can fit the same 1.1-1.7 micron transmission data equally well.
assumptions: the adopted patchy-cloud geometry is representative
the synthetic atmospheres capture the relevant opacities
the WFC3 bandpass and noise level are representative
uncertainty: The exact degeneracy is limited to certain wavelength regions, especially the WFC3 bandpass.

claim_text: The HST/WFC3 spectra of HD 189733 b and HAT-P-11 b can be explained by solar-composition atmospheres with patchy clouds without requiring high mean molecular weight or globally uniform clouds.
supporting_evidence: Atmospheric retrievals of the two observed WFC3 spectra achieve good fits with partially cloudy solar-composition models.
assumptions: the patchy-cloud retrieval parameterization captures the dominant limb structure
stellar contamination and instrument systematics are controlled
the observed wavelength range contains enough information for the model comparison
uncertainty: The spectra are also subject to the cloud-composition degeneracy, so broader observations are needed to distinguish alternatives.

claim_text: Rayleigh-scattering differences or ingress-egress residuals can break the degeneracy between patchy solar-composition clouds and high-mean-molecular-weight atmospheres.
supporting_evidence: The models predict distinct molecular Rayleigh-scattering behavior and an approximately 100 ppm partially cloudy-limb signature in ingress and egress when transit timing is known to seconds.
assumptions: transit timing can be measured to second-level precision
instrumental precision is sufficient to resolve about 100 ppm residuals
the cloud asymmetry remains stable during transit
uncertainty: The ingress-egress diagnostic is conditional on accurately known transit timing and adequate photometric precision.

claim_text: Exo-Transmit provides an open-source forward model that can generate transmission spectra across a wide range of exoplanet sizes, gravities, temperatures, compositions, clouds, and hazes.
supporting_evidence: The package supports hot Jupiters through rocky super-Earths and includes configurable atmospheric composition, temperature, gravity, radius, cloud deck pressure, and enhanced Rayleigh scattering.
assumptions: the one-dimensional transmission formalism and included opacities are adequate for the intended applications
users provide physically meaningful input atmospheres
uncertainty: The abstract presents software capability rather than a quantified accuracy benchmark against observations.

claim_text: Two analytic signal-to-noise metrics can prioritize TESS planet candidates for transmission and thermal-emission atmospheric characterization.
supporting_evidence: The authors derive separate transmission and emission spectroscopy metrics and calibrate threshold values using a simulated TESS detection catalog.
assumptions: the analytic scaling relations approximate observatory performance
the simulated TESS population is representative
candidate masses and stellar parameters are known well enough for ranking
uncertainty: The thresholds are based on simulated detections and pre-launch assumptions about follow-up facilities.

claim_text: Applying the proposed metric thresholds to simulated TESS detections yields an estimated sample of about 300 high-quality atmospheric-characterization targets across multiple planet-size bins.
supporting_evidence: Thresholds selected from the Sullivan et al. simulated catalog retain approximately 300 candidates extending from sub-Jovians to Earth-size potentially habitable worlds.
assumptions: the simulated TESS yield and target properties are representative
follow-up confirmation and mass measurements can be obtained
JWST and later facilities have the assumed capabilities
uncertainty: The sample size is a forecast based on simulations rather than an observed TESS catalog.

claim_text: Typical stellar heterogeneity in inactive FGK dwarfs is unlikely to produce detectable molecular-band contamination in transmission spectra, whereas active G and K hosts can produce detectable visual slopes and line-region effects.
supporting_evidence: Rotating photosphere models across F, G, and K activity levels predict low spot coverage for inactive stars, detectable slopes for typical active G and K dwarfs, and appreciable Na D offsets from unocculted faculae in K dwarfs.
assumptions: the adopted spot and facula temperature contrasts are representative
photometric variability maps to plausible covering fractions
the modeled stellar spectra capture relevant line and continuum effects
uncertainty: The conclusion depends strongly on activity level and spectral type; late-K TiO/VO contamination may remain detectable.

claim_text: Helios-r2 retrievals can recover surface gravities for benchmark brown dwarfs that agree with previous studies or dynamical-mass constraints.
supporting_evidence: Retrievals of GJ 570 D and Epsilon Indi Ba and Bb yield surface gravities consistent with literature values and, for the Epsilon Indi companions, values inferred from dynamical masses.
assumptions: the medium-resolution spectra and adopted opacities contain enough gravity information
the retrieval priors do not dominate the result
the benchmark dynamical constraints are accurate
uncertainty: The agreement is strongest where dynamical masses exist and does not resolve radius-related degeneracies.

claim_text: Retrieved brown-dwarf radii and masses can be unphysical or model dependent, and inferred carbon-to-oxygen ratio and metallicity depend on whether chemical equilibrium is assumed.
supporting_evidence: Cross-model mock tests show that calibration factors can absorb modeling discrepancies, while benchmark retrievals lack a clear rejection criterion for unphysical radii and change composition results under different chemistry assumptions.
assumptions: the tested model mismatches are representative of real retrieval systematics
the calibration factor behaves similarly on observed spectra
uncertainty: The paper explicitly cautions that radii and derived masses should be treated with great care and that chemistry assumptions alter C/O and metallicity.

claim_text: Small sub-micron condensate particles can produce prominent infrared vibrational features accompanied by an optical scattering slope in hot-Jupiter transmission spectra.
supporting_evidence: Computed optical-to-infrared transmission spectra across condensate species, grain sizes, and distributions show strong vibrational-mode absorption for small particles and associated optical slopes.
assumptions: the chosen condensate species and particle-size distributions are representative
the cloud particles are sufficiently abundant and vertically distributed to affect transmission
the forward scattering treatment is adequate
uncertainty: Broad spectra may not distinguish individual condensates even when vibrational bond families are discernible.

claim_text: Long-wavelength vibrational features may distinguish condensate-cloud formation from photochemical-haze scenarios even when individual cloud species remain degenerate.
supporting_evidence: The modeled spectra associate different vibrational bonds with condensate families and show that these features are accessible at longer wavelengths relevant to JWST.
assumptions: JWST precision and wavelength coverage are sufficient
different cloud-formation pathways produce measurably distinct bond signatures
other atmospheric opacity sources do not erase the diagnostic
uncertainty: The paper presents this as a potential discriminant rather than a guaranteed identification of individual condensates.

claim_text: HST/WFC3 transmission spectroscopy detects the 1.4 micron water band in WASP-121 b at high confidence.
supporting_evidence: A primary transit observed from 1.12 to 1.64 microns with HST/WFC3 yields a 5.4 sigma water-band detection.
assumptions: instrumental and stellar systematics are adequately corrected
the 1.4 micron feature is correctly attributed to water
uncertainty: The detection significance is reported as 5.4 sigma.

claim_text: The deeper optical transits of WASP-121 b are unlikely to be caused by high-altitude haze alone and are consistent with additional TiO and VO opacity.
supporting_evidence: Reanalyzed B, r-prime, and z-prime light curves show significantly deeper optical transits than the near-infrared spectrum, while haze-only scattering does not reproduce the difference.
assumptions: the optical and infrared transit depths are on a consistent absolute scale
stellar variability does not drive the optical excess
the TiO/VO opacity models are applicable
uncertainty: The result is described as evidence rather than a confirmed molecular detection; enhanced 1.12-1.3 micron opacity may instead or additionally involve FeH.

claim_text: PandExo reproduces independent noise simulations and prior HST performance to within approximately 10 percent across HST/WFC3 and all supported JWST instruments.
supporting_evidence: The package is benchmarked against each JWST instrument team's independent simulator and previous HST observations, with reported agreement within 10 percent.
assumptions: the external simulators and prior HST data provide suitable reference standards
the compared observing configurations are aligned
pre-launch JWST detector assumptions are representative
uncertainty: The benchmark reflects pre-launch instrument models and reports agreement at the approximately 10 percent level.

claim_text: Laboratory simulations show that all tested super-Earth and mini-Neptune atmospheric compositions produce haze particles, but with production rates spanning orders of magnitude.
supporting_evidence: Experiments covering 300-600 K and 100 to 10,000 times solar metallicity produce particles in every case, with measured rates from 0.04 mg/h to about 10 mg/h.
assumptions: the laboratory energy source and gas mixtures are relevant analogues for exoplanet photochemistry
measured particle production rates scale meaningfully to planetary atmospheres
uncertainty: The experiments cover a finite composition-temperature grid and do not directly predict global aerosol optical depth.

claim_text: Cooler 1,000-times-solar, water-dominated or methane-rich atmospheres can produce haze at rates exceeding the authors' Titan reference experiment.
supporting_evidence: The 300 K and 400 K experiments at 1,000 times solar metallicity reach about 10 mg/h compared with 7.4 mg/h for the Titan simulation.
assumptions: the Titan experiment is an appropriate comparative baseline
laboratory production-rate differences reflect atmospheric chemistry rather than apparatus-specific effects
uncertainty: High production is limited to some tested conditions; other atmospheres produce far less haze.

claim_text: For aerosol-free TRAPPIST-1 planets, JWST/NIRSpec Prism transmission spectroscopy could detect carbon-dioxide-containing terrestrial atmospheres in fewer than ten transits.
supporting_evidence: Simulations of plausible post-ocean-loss and habitable atmospheres across JWST time-series modes identify NIRSpec Prism as optimal and predict fewer than ten transits for all seven planets when high-altitude aerosols are absent.
assumptions: the modeled atmospheres are representative
on-orbit JWST noise matches the simulations
stellar contamination and systematics can be controlled
high-altitude aerosols are absent
uncertainty: Venus-like sulfuric-acid aerosols can increase the required transit count by up to a factor of twelve.

claim_text: Water and biogenic oxygen or ozone would be extremely difficult to detect in plausible TRAPPIST-1 atmospheres, while abiotic oxygen from past ocean loss may be more accessible through collision-induced oxygen or near-infrared ozone features.
supporting_evidence: Simulated transmission and emission observations show weak water sensitivity at the altitudes probed, severe difficulty for biogenic O2 and O3, and potentially detectable O2-O2 features at 1.06 and 1.27 microns or near-infrared O3 for selected planets.
assumptions: the adopted atmospheric evolutionary scenarios are representative
the modeled molecular opacities and cloud assumptions are accurate
stellar and instrumental systematics permit the simulated sensitivity
uncertainty: Detectability varies by planet and atmospheric state; the claim is a forecast from simulations.

claim_text: The combined HARPS-N and CARMENES transmission spectra of HD 209458 b show no detectable sodium absorption once center-to-limb variation and the Rossiter-McLaughlin effect are modeled.
supporting_evidence: Five transit observations around the sodium region, examined individually and jointly, are reproduced by stellar center-to-limb and Rossiter-McLaughlin models without adding planetary sodium absorption.
assumptions: the center-to-limb and Rossiter-McLaughlin models are accurate
telluric and instrumental systematics are controlled
the combined data retain sensitivity to a planetary sodium signal
uncertainty: The non-detection contrasts with prior literature detections and is limited by the signal-to-noise of the available nights.

claim_text: Some previously reported high-resolution atmospheric detections may require revision because stellar center-to-limb variation and Rossiter-McLaughlin signatures can mimic planetary absorption.
supporting_evidence: The same modeled stellar effects explain the sodium region, H-alpha, Ca II infrared triplet, Mg I triplet, and K I D1 measurements of HD 209458 b without invoking atmospheric absorption.
assumptions: the modeled stellar line-shape effects generalize to prior analyses
differences in reduction pipelines do not explain the disagreement
the benchmark system is representative of other vulnerable systems
uncertainty: The authors state the concern applies strongly to some star-planet systems but that the effects are small in others.

claim_text: A two-stage hybrid temperature-pressure retrieval can combine the convergence robustness of a parametric profile with the accuracy of a layer-by-layer profile for exoplanet emission spectra.
supporting_evidence: The Tau-REx emission framework first retrieves an analytic temperature-pressure profile and then refines it with individual atmospheric layers in simulations and observed secondary-eclipse examples.
assumptions: the analytic first stage converges near a physically relevant solution
the layer-by-layer refinement is identifiable from the available spectrum
the radiative-transfer and opacity models are adequate
uncertainty: The abstract demonstrates the method on simulated WASP-76 b and 55 Cnc e spectra plus HD 189733 b measurements but does not give a single aggregate accuracy metric.

claim_text: High-dispersion transmission spectroscopy detects carbon monoxide and water vapor in HD 189733 b and yields a rotation rate consistent with tidal locking.
supporting_evidence: A CRIRES transit spectrum at resolving power near 100,000 gives a 7.6 sigma cross-correlation signal maximized at rotational velocity 3.4(+1.3,-2.1) km/s, corresponding to a 1.7(+2.9,-0.4) day period consistent with the 2.2 day orbit.
assumptions: the cross-correlation templates accurately represent the planetary spectrum
stellar and Rossiter-McLaughlin residuals are removed
line broadening is correctly attributed to rotation and winds
uncertainty: The data only marginally prefer rotating over non-rotating models at 1.5 sigma, although periods shorter than one day are excluded at 3 sigma.

claim_text: The near-infrared data indicate a small day-to-night wind in HD 189733 b and, when compared with a much larger optical sodium blueshift, imply strong vertical wind shear.
supporting_evidence: The CRIRES retrieval gives a day-to-night wind of -1.7(+1.1,-1.2) km/s, while comparison with a published sodium blueshift of 8 plus or minus 2 km/s samples a different atmospheric pressure regime.
assumptions: the near-infrared and sodium measurements are both free of major systematics
the two tracers probe meaningfully different altitudes
differences in line formation can be interpreted as vertical wind shear
uncertainty: The near-infrared wind measurement is small and model dependent; the shear inference depends on comparison with an external sodium result.
